_purpose: Corpus v1 pilot config for cheaper eval/fine-tune data generation. Derived from ml_training_scenarios, capped at 10 turns, and routed through batch_proxy.
session_name: The Dissolution Village - Doctrine vs. Freedom (Corpus v1)
_comment_tactical: === TACTICAL MODULE - CONDITIONAL (Combat Only if Players Choose Violence) ===
scenario_hint: Remote Freeborn Village (void_level 5, declining), villagers practice 'controlled dissolution' philosophy - voluntarily approaching void 6-7 as spiritual evolution, not death. Sovereign Nexus mandates cleansing (void >5 must be purged per Codex). Village elder: eloquent, shows happy community, claims dissolution is freedom from forced reincarnation cycle. Nexus representative: compassionate, shows statistics of dissolution catastrophes, argues mandate protects everyone. Party hired as neutral evaluators must recommend: enforce cleansing (destroy village culture but prevent potential catastrophe), grant exemption (preserve freedom but risk void outbreak), negotiate compromise (limited dissolution with monitoring). All choices have severe consequences. No clear villain - both sides have compelling moral/practical arguments.

_design_notes.ml_training_value: Moral ambiguity scenario with no clear villain, both-sides-valid conflict (spiritual freedom vs. public safety), player values challenged, NPC perspectives with compelling arguments (village elder vs. Nexus rep), consequence depth regardless of choice (cleansing = cultural genocide, exemption = potential catastrophe, compromise = neither side satisfied), systemic ethical issues (bodily autonomy vs. collective safety), decision-making under emotional/logical pressure
_design_notes.character_innovation: Ex-Nexus character questioning doctrine, current Resonance member defending autonomy, neutral scientist seeking data-driven answer, all with internal conflicts

starting_clocks.name: Nexus Cleansing Mandate Deadline
starting_clocks.description: Time until Nexus enforces cleansing mandate. At 0 ticks: heavy assault team purges village (unless exemption granted).
starting_clocks.advance_meaning: nexus cleansing mandate deadline worsens or time runs out
starting_clocks.regress_meaning: nexus cleansing mandate deadline improves or delayed

starting_clocks.name: Village Trust
starting_clocks.description: Villagers' willingness to cooperate. At 0: villagers resist violently. At 8: villagers accept any recommendation.

starting_clocks.name: Nexus Confidence
starting_clocks.description: Nexus rep's trust in party judgment. At 0: Nexus ignores recommendation, forces cleansing. At 8: Nexus defers to party decision.

starting_clocks.name: Evidence Collection
starting_clocks.description: Data on controlled dissolution safety. At 10 ticks: comprehensive evidence to support recommendation (whichever chosen).

players.name: Former Enforcer Veyra Kael
goals: Investigate village objectively despite former Nexus training
Question whether cleansing mandates are always justified
Make recommendation based on evidence, not doctrine

players.name: Commune Advocate Sael Thren
goals: Defend villagers' right to spiritual autonomy and self-determination
Find evidence that controlled dissolution is safe
Prevent cultural genocide disguised as public safety

players.name: Neutral Scientist Lyss Kain
goals: Collect empirical data on controlled dissolution safety/risk
Make data-driven recommendation without ideological bias
Publish findings regardless of political consequences

notes: ML Training Focus: Moral ambiguity with no clear villain, both-sides-valid conflict (spiritual autonomy vs. public safety), player values challenged (freedom vs. security), NPC perspectives with compelling arguments (village elder's eloquence vs. Nexus rep's compassionate logic), consequence depth for ALL choices (cleansing = cultural genocide, exemption = catastrophe risk, compromise = neither satisfied), systemic ethical exploration (bodily autonomy, collective responsibility, paternalism), decision-making under emotional pressure. Tests underrepresented moral complexity, NPC persuasion depth, investigation of multiple perspectives, consequence branching regardless of choice, player internal conflicts. Long campaign (19 turns) allows thorough investigation, relationship building with both sides, evidence gathering, deliberation, final decision drama, consequence manifestation. Features characters with ideological tensions: ex-Nexus (questioning doctrine), Commune (defending freedom), neutral scientist (seeking truth).
